title: Fan Curve Explorer
description: Plotly chart of two illustrative fans' pressure and BHP curves with a six-question check that asks the learner to differentiate stall-region from stable operating points and overloading from non-overloading power curves.
creator: Twin City Fan
subject: fan curve
stall region
brake horsepower
non-overloading power curve
overloading power curve
rights: Copyright 2026 Twin City Fan. All rights reserved.

educational.audience: Adult professional development: application engineers, sales staff, representatives and specifying engineers
educational.topic: Fan curves, stall region and power curves
learningObjectives: Differentiate stable from stall-region operating points by locating each point relative to the pressure-curve peak
Differentiate overloading from non-overloading power curves by reading the shape of the BHP curve
Read the maximum BHP of a non-overloading curve as the motor size that cannot be overloaded at that speed

accessibility.notes: Chart region has an aria-label; verdicts announced through FP.announce (aria-live) and shown in a role=status feedback box; ✓/✗ glyphs, solid/dashed borders and round/square chart markers pair with colour; keys 1 and 2 choose an answer, Enter submits, goes to the next question and starts over.

controls.label: Yes / No, Curve A / Curve B
Highest BHP
controls.purpose: Type the question 6 answer in BHP

controls.label: Next question / See score
controls.purpose: Go to the next question or the score (Enter)

controls.purpose: Clear the marks and the score and return to question 1

rules: Stall region for Curve A: airflow < 4,000 CFM
Stall region for Curve B: airflow < 8,000 CFM
A curve is non-overloading when its BHP has a maximum inside the plotted range and decreases after it; it is overloading when BHP increases at every listed step
Question 6 is correct when the typed value is within ±0.1 of 9.5 BHP
assumptions: One fixed speed per fan, standard air
Points are joined by straight lines between the listed values
limitations: Curves are illustrative, not catalog ratings

sources: Illustrative curves shaped after typical backward inclined (Curve A) and forward curved (Curve B) centrifugal fan behavior; not Twin City Fan published ratings. Data served by the kit's fan-curves.js (FP.curves.A, FP.curves.B).

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Hover-to-read exploration followed by committed answers with immediate feedback
keyQuestions: Is 3,000 CFM on Curve A in the stall region?
Is 9,000 CFM on Curve A in the stall region?
Is 6,000 CFM on Curve B in the stall region?
Is 11,000 CFM on Curve B in the stall region?
Which curve has a non-overloading power curve?
What is the highest BHP anywhere on Curve A?
commonMisconceptions: Any point the pressure curve passes through is a safe operating point, including points left of the peak
A fan's BHP always rises with airflow
The highest-pressure point is the best place to select a fan
assessmentOpportunities: Score shown as 'n of 6 correct' (running line 'Questions correct: n of 6'); mastery is 5 of 6 on the first attempt; question 6 is correct within 0.1 of 9.5 BHP.
